topics.name: 3.1 Business in the real world
points: 3.1.1 The purpose and nature of businesses: why businesses exist, goods and services, needs and wants
3.1.1 Factors of production, opportunity cost and the three sectors of industry
3.1.1 Enterprise and entrepreneurs; the dynamic nature of business
3.1.2 Business ownership: sole traders, partnerships, private and public limited companies, not-for-profit organisations
3.1.2 Limited and unlimited liability; choosing a legal structure
3.1.3 Setting business aims and objectives and how they change; measuring success
3.1.4 Stakeholders: objectives, impact of business activity, influence and conflict
3.1.5 Business location: factors influencing location
3.1.6 Business planning: purpose and sections of a business plan
3.1.6 Fixed, variable and total costs; revenue, profit and loss
3.1.7 Expanding a business: organic growth (franchising, new outlets, e-commerce), outsourcing, mergers and takeovers
3.1.7 Economies and diseconomies of scale; average unit costs

topics.name: 3.2 Influences on business
points: 3.2.1 Technology: e-commerce and digital communication
3.2.2 Ethical considerations
3.2.2 Environmental considerations and sustainability
3.2.3 The economic climate: interest rates, level of employment and consumer spending
3.2.4 Globalisation: competing internationally; exchange rates
3.2.5 Legislation: employment law (minimum and living wage, Equality Act 2010)
3.2.5 Legislation: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and consumer law
3.2.6 The competitive environment: competitive markets, uncertainty and risk

papers.name: Paper 1 Influences of operations and HRM on business activity

topics.name: 3.3 Business operations
points: 3.3.1 Production processes: job and flow production
3.3.1 Efficiency in production: lean production and just in time
3.3.2 Procurement: managing stock (JIT and JIC) and choosing suppliers
3.3.2 Effects of procurement and logistics; supply chain management
3.3.3 The concept of quality: consequences of quality issues and total quality management
3.3.3 Costs and benefits of maintaining quality
3.3.4 Good customer service: methods, benefits and dangers of poor service
3.3.4 ICT and customer service: websites, e-commerce and social media

topics.name: 3.4 Human resources
points: 3.4.1 Organisational structures and their appropriateness
3.4.1 Centralisation and decentralisation
3.4.2 The need for recruitment; methods of recruitment and selection
3.4.2 Contracts of employment
3.4.3 Importance of motivation and methods to motivate staff
3.4.4 Importance of training and types of training

papers.name: Paper 2 Influences of marketing and finance on business activity

topics.name: 3.5 Marketing
points: 3.5.1 Identifying and understanding customers
3.5.2 Market segmentation
3.5.3 Purpose of market research; primary and secondary methods
3.5.3 Qualitative and quantitative research; using findings; market size and market share
3.5.4 Price: pricing methods and factors influencing pricing
3.5.4 Product: new products, design, USP and brand image
3.5.4 Product: the product life cycle, extension strategies and the Boston Matrix
3.5.4 Promotion: methods and factors influencing the promotional mix
3.5.4 Place: distribution channels, e-commerce and m-commerce
3.5.4 Integrating the marketing mix and how it changes over time

topics.name: 3.6 Finance
points: 3.6.1 Sources of finance and their appropriateness
3.6.2 Importance of cash; interpreting cash flow forecasts; cash versus profit
3.6.3 Basic financial terms and calculations
3.6.3 Average rate of return
3.6.3 Break-even
3.6.4 Financial statements: purpose, components and interpretation
